property_summary: A successful call to transfer must return true, but the buggy version returns false.
For any valid non-empty _tos array and matching v array, a successful call to transfer must return true, but the buggy version returns false.
For any non-empty _tos and matching v arrays and a caddress that is an EOA (no code), the call to transfer succeeds and returns true in the reference, but the mutant returns false.
For any valid call to C.transfer that completes successfully, the return value must equal the result of (v[i] > 0 ? true : false) for the last loop iteration, but the mutant always returns false.

The reference contract ensures that every external call in the loop succeeds by checking the return value of the low-level call; the mutant omits this check, causing the transaction to succeed even when an external call fails.

For any valid input, the reference contract guarantees that the transfer invocation does not revert (returns true), whereas the mutant allows the invocation to succeed even when an external call fails, thereby differing in the revert/success behavior observable via the call's return boolean.

For any admissible input, if the reference contract's transfer call succeeds, then every external transferFrom call must have succeeded; the bug violates this because it ignores individual call failures, causing transfer to return true even when some inner calls fail.

For any admissible input, if any inner transferFrom call fails, the reference transfer call reverts (returns false observable via catch), while the mutant ignores the failure and succeeds (returns true); the bug violates this by not requiring each inner call to succeed.
